candidates.name: Stockholm Cathedral
candidates.price: Entrance 40 kr except for visitors to services 21 May-29 Sep, free entry rest of year
candidates.hours: Open daily 09:00-18:00 21 May-29 Sep, 09:00-16:00 rest of year. Guided tours every Thu at 11
candidates.content: Storkyrkan is the oldest church in Gamla stan. Built in the 13th century in the Gothic style, the exterior was remodelled in Baroque style around 1740. The church is the seat of the Church of Sweden bishop of Stockholm. It contain

candidates.name: Riddarholmen Church
candidates.content: Riddarholm is the ancient core of Stockholm and this is the city's oldest building - though no longer the oldest church, as it's nowadays simply a museum. Built as an abbey in the late 14th century. Many Swedish monarchs are burie

candidates.name: German Church
candidates.price: Entrance 40 kr except for visitors to services 21 May-29 Sep, free entry rest of year
candidates.content: Officially named Sankta Gertrud, this Gamla stan church is the home of the first German-speaking parish outside Germany, giving some clue to the importance of German merchants in the history of Stockholm. On the site of the church

candidates.name: Royal Palace
candidates.content: At times referred to by Swedes at the "Royal Castle". Built between 1697 and 1754, dominating the north-eastern part of the Old Town, the Royal Palace is the official residence of the monarch of Sweden. However, the Royal family l

candidates.name: The Royal Armoury
candidates.content: Located in the Royal Palace, still an independent museum. In 1628, King Gustavus II Adolphus declared that his uniform from the Thirty Years War campaign in Poland should be put on display for eternity. Since then, the Royal Armou

candidates.name: Stockholm City Hall
candidates.price: Public daily tours run several times a day, 110 kr. Tours to the City Hall Tower run about 10 times a day May–September, 50 kr, tickets are only sold on the day of the visit
candidates.content: The city hall, where the Nobel Prize Banquet takes place every year, is an imposing brick building in the city centre. Guided tours are held daily, and allow you to see the impressive halls used for the Nobel festivities, the Blue

candidates.name: National Museum of Fine Arts
candidates.hours: Summer Tue-Sun 11-18, Sat 11-17, Non-Summer T-Wed 11-17, Thu 11-20, Fri-Sun 11-17
candidates.content: Sweden's national museum for European art opened in 1866. A renovation for accessibility and climate control was finished in 2018. The museum exhibits works by Rembrandt, Rubens, Goya, Renoir, Degas and Gauguin, as well as well-kn

candidates.name: Stockholm City Museum
candidates.content: This building was finished in the 1660s, as Stockholm's Southern City Hall. Over the centuries, it has been used as a courthouse, a jail, an anatomic theatre, and a school. Since 1942 it is a museum, displaying Stockholm's history

candidates.name: Swedish History Museum
candidates.content: The history of Sweden from the Ice Age (10,000 BC) to present day, with emphasis on the Middle Ages (11th to 16th centuries). The exhibition on the Viking Age was expanded in 2021. In the Gold Room, you'll find gold treasures from

candidates.name: Army Museum
candidates.content: Displays the history of war, focused on the rise and fall of the Swedish Empire during the 16th to 18th centuries, followed by Sweden's role in the shade of World War I, World War II in Europe and Cold War Europe. The museum makes

candidates.name: Vasa Museum
candidates.content: This museum displays the Vasa, an original warship built for the Thirty Years War which sank in Stockholm Harbour on its maiden voyage in 1628, during the heyday of the Swedish Empire. Salvaged in 1961, the ship is almost wholly p

candidates.name: Skansen
candidates.hours: 1 May-20 Jun: daily 10:00-20:00, 21 Jun-31 Aug: 10:00-22:00, shorter hours the rest of the year, but always at least 10:00-15:00
candidates.content: Founded in 1891, Skansen is the world's oldest open-air museum, containing a zoological garden specializing in Nordic fauna, such as moose, reindeer, bear, wolf, lynx and wolverine. It features over 150 historic buildings from pre

candidates.name: Nordiska Museet
candidates.hours: Daily 10:00-17:00 year round; Sep-May: also Wed 10:00-20:00
candidates.content: A museum of cultural history from 1520 to our days, in an impressive 1907 cathedral-like building on Djurgården. Exhibitions focus on Swedish handicraft, customs and traditions. See Nordic folk culture for context.

candidates.name: Abba The Museum
candidates.hours: Mid-Jan to May, Sep to mid-Dec: Mon Tue Fri-Sun 10:00-18:00, Wed Thu 10:00-20:00; Jun to Aug: daily 09:00-20:00; 10:00-18:00; mid-Dec to Dec 21: daily 10:00-18:00
candidates.content: A museum of the Swedish pop band ABBA: their spectacular costumes, gold records and original items. In the same building you’ll find Pop House Hotel with 49 stylishly decorated hotel rooms and Pop House Hotel Food & Bar. It has a

candidates.name: Biological Museum
candidates.content: Scandinavian and Arctic dioramas with stuffed Scandinavian animals, lit only by daylight (limiting the opening hours; the museum closes at 15:00 in October-March, and 16:00 in April-September). When built in 1893, the diorama tech

candidates.name: Christina Gyllenstierna statue
candidates.content: Kristina Nilsdotter (Gyllenstierna) led Sweden's uprising against Denmark in the 1510s, after the death of her husband Sten Sture (Sweden's acting head of state). The statue was erected on the Stockholm Palace courtyard in 1912, a

candidates.name: Stortorget
candidates.content: Stockholm's oldest square, dated back to the 13th century. While the square was used for corporal punishment during most of its history, the most infamous event was the 1520 Stockholm Bloodbath, where Danish king Kristian II (who

candidates.name: Forum för levande historia
candidates.content: A museum with exhibitions focused on human rights and crimes against humanity. Previous exhibitions have depicted Sweden's role in World War II in Europe and the Holocaust.

candidates.name: Klara Church
candidates.content: Close to the Sergels Torg square, and one of the few buildings in the district to survive the 1960s redevelopment, this large redbrick church was built in the 16th century, following the demolition of a 13th-century nunnery. The 1

candidates.name: Adolf Fredrik's church
candidates.content: Adolf Fredrik's church, named by King Adolf Fredrik, was built in 1768-1774. The exterior is quite intact, while the interior was radically changed in the 1890s. In the church, there is a monument to the philosopher René Descartes

candidates.name: Mediterranean Museum
candidates.content: Contains ancient artefacts of the Mediterranean and the Middle East, with a distinguished collection from Cyprus, and an Egyptian mummy exhibition.

candidates.name: Kungsträdgården metro station
candidates.content: [ˈkɵŋsˌtrɛˈgoːɖən] Opened in 1977, and is known for its art, with elements from the former palace Makalös and other demolished buildings in the neighborhood. Due to the 1971 protests, construction was delayed, and the eastern exit

candidates.name: Hallwyll Museum
candidates.content: A museum of antiquities, many of them owned by Swedish royals and nobles. Guided tours in Swedish and English available. Note that some parts of the museum can only be accessed on a guided tour.

candidates.name: Museum of Modern Art
candidates.content: Stockholm's museum of modern art is headed by Lars Nittve, formerly of London's Tate Modern. These museums have several works by famous artists - Pablo Picasso, Henri Matisse, Salvador Dalí and Irving Penn, an American photographe

candidates.name: East Asian Museum
candidates.content: Displays ancient, classical and contemporary East Asian culture.

candidates.name: Ivar Lo-museet
candidates.content: A museum for Swedish writer and labour activist Ivar Lo-Johansson, famous for depicting Swedish farm workers' harsh conditions. The museum contains a small exhibition and Lo-Johansson's apartment, and requires advance booking. A s

candidates.name: Mojang Studios
candidates.content: Headquarters of Swedish video game developer studio, best known for developing the sandbox and survival game Minecraft, the best-selling video game of all time.

candidates.name: Stockholm Public Library
candidates.content: A 1928 building in art nouveau style with a flair of early functionalism, designed by the famous Swedish architect Erik Gunnar Asplund. The interior of the cylinder-shaped main hall is spectacular, with three floors of bookshelves

candidates.name: Gröna Lund
candidates.hours: Open at least noon-23:00 most days June-August, shorter hours in May and early September
candidates.content: Djurgården has Stockholm's only amusement park, with more or less standard attractions and games. The restaurants in the park are expensive and generally far from a culinary experience. No rides are included in the entrance fee. A

candidates.name: The Royal Swedish Opera
candidates.content: This 1898 building, stages classical operas in original language or Swedish, as well as classical ballets and concerts. The first opera house was built in 1782, commissioned by King Gustav III; 10 years later he was assassinated a

candidates.name: Strawberry Arena
candidates.content: A 50,000-seat stadium for association football games and other events, opened in October 2012. The arena hosts the men's national football team, as well as AIK. As of 2015, parking and roads are undeveloped, and traffic tends to b

candidates.name: Hop On - Hop Off Boat
candidates.content: Audio track in 11 languages. Two of the most frequented stops are at the Palace, and at the Gamla Stan, right across the canal from T Slussen. The recordings on this loop service are reasonably informative.

candidates.name: Under the bridges of Stockholm
candidates.content: Departing from Strömkajen by Grand Hôtel and opposite the Royal Castle (T Kungsträdgården), this tour on both the sea and on lake Mälaren passes under 15 bridges and through two locks. Several departures every day, depending on th

candidates.name: Kungsträdgården
candidates.content: A park with frequent stage performances, and ice skating during winter.

candidates.name: Stockholm Concert Hall
candidates.content: The home stage of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, and the place of the annual Nobel Prize ceremony.

candidates.name: Royal Canal Tour
candidates.content: Departs from Strömkajen and takes you around the eastern parts of the city, passing through the lush Djurgården canal. 50 min.

candidates.name: Historical Canal Tour
candidates.content: Departs from Stadshusbron next to the City Hall (T T-Centralen), and passes Kungsholmen and other western islands of the city. 50 min.

candidates.name: Stockholm Grand Tour
candidates.content: Combines a boat and a bus tour. 3 hours 30 min, 450 kr.

candidates.name: Storkyrkobadet
candidates.price: Adults 40 kr, includes entrance to pool and sauna. Students and seniors 30 kr
candidates.hours: Open for men Tue Fri Sun 05:00-20:30; for women Mon Thu 05:00-20:30; closed during summer
candidates.content: A small secret hidden in what once was a wine cellar in the old town, where you can take a bath beneath 18th century vaults. Men and women cannot visit the bath together.

candidates.name: Solvalla
candidates.content: For a day at the races, you can go to Stockholm's hippodrome Solvalla, watch trotters compete in harness racing, and place some bets. Races are held Wednesday nights and many weekends. The biggest event is the prestigious Elitlopp

candidates.name: Stockholm Panorama
candidates.content: A tour of some major sights that departs from Gustaf Adolf Torg (T T-Centralen). 1 hour 30 min, 300 kr.

candidates.name: Junibacken
candidates.content: Astrid Lindgren, author of Pippi Longstocking, Karlsson-on-the-Roof and numerous other children's books, is by far Sweden's most popular writer of children's books. Located on the island Djurgården, like many other child-friendly

candidates.name: Rooftop Tour
candidates.content: Look at Stockholm from the roofs of Riddarholmen island. An exciting experience if you're not afraid of heights.

candidates.name: Old Town Walking Tour
candidates.content: Daily walking tours of Gamla Stan.

candidates.name: Centralbadet
candidates.content: A classical bath-house in one of Stockholm's most beautiful art nouveau buildings, this is a place where you can go for a swim, have a beer in the sauna bar or enjoy a full spa treatment. Rather expensive and sometimes crowded on

candidates.name: Oscarsteatern
candidates.content: An art nouveau playhouse opened in 1906, which usually stages Swedish and international musicals.

candidates.name: Victoria
candidates.content: On the lively Götgatan street, this beautiful 1930s theatre screens a broad variety of Hollywood blockbusters and classic movies ranging from the birth of cinema and onwards.

candidates.name: Rio
candidates.content: Amidst the bars of the Hornstull district, this charming independent theatre, neighbouring the LGBT-friendly café Copacabana, arranges screenings of films of all sorts - from 3D-features to festivals of low-budget shorts.

candidates.name: Stampen
candidates.content: Popular Jazz club which has been around since 1965, there's live music almost every night.

candidates.name: Sjöstaden Skybar
candidates.content: A restaurant on the 28th floor with an astounding view of Stockholm.

candidates.name: Systembolaget
candidates.hours: Generally open Mon-Wed 10:00-18:00, Thu-Fri 10:00-19:00, Sat 10:00-15:00, all stores closed Sun
candidates.content: Systembolaget is the government monopoly chain for selling alcohol. The stores have a wide assortment and helpful, knowledgeable staff. Tax makes beer and hard liquor expensive. Surprisingly, high-end wines can be a bargain. Centr

candidates.name: Regeringsgatan
candidates.content: The largest Systembolaget store in Stockholm, with a special selection of exclusive wines

candidates.name: 6e Tunnan
candidates.content: Medieval bar and restaurant, with medieval food and mead, and a small heavy-metal bar at street level. Live performances most evenings, usually Medieval-style or rock music.

candidates.name: O'Connell's Irish Pub
candidates.content: This comfortable and cosy Irish pub serves excellent pub food and has live music most nights of the week. Be sure to check out the 400-year old cellar bar.

candidates.name: Dovas
candidates.content: Cheap beer, 30 kr for a 500 ml bottle of Norrlands Guld or another local ale. There is a nightclub opposite which most of the young locals seem to disappear into when this place closes.

candidates.name: Radisson Skybar
candidates.content: Not the most elevated sky bar in the world, in any sense of the word, but if you want a panoramic view to go with your drink this is the only option in the Norrmalm area (although Gondolen's Bar on Södermalm probably has better dr

candidates.name: Glenn Miller Café
candidates.content: Renowned jazz club in Stockholm serving French cuisine. There is a live jazz concert in the late evenings, Wednesday through Sunday. Reservations are available for dining guests and the concert fee is a minimum of 50 kr per s

candidates.name: East
candidates.content: Asian cross-cooking, funky music, and ethnic diversity hardly seen at any other nightclub in central Stockholm. Open until 03:00 every night, but gets crowded, so go there well before midnight. Dress code may apply.

candidates.name: The Cadier Bar
candidates.content: Inside the Grand Hôtel, this is one of the more upscale places one can find in Stockholm. It has been refurbished, and offers a modern yet classic atmosphere and really good drinks at that.

candidates.name: Berns Bar
candidates.content: Berns Bar is one of the trendier hangouts in the city centre, with a nice lounge and several dancefloors. You can eat a late dinner here to avoid the high entrance fee. Otherwise, make sure to show up early (before 23:00) in order

candidates.name: Akkurat
candidates.content: Friendly English-style pub offering good food, real ale, plenty of beers from all over the world as well as 450 different whiskies. A place where younger and older drinkers meet.

candidates.name: Södra Teatern Bar
candidates.content: Open Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights, this very relaxed and stylish bar offers a marvellous view of Stockholm from its lounge. Be sure to come before 23:00 to get seats offering the best view.

candidates.name: Grillska huset
candidates.content: The medieval building was owned by the Grill family from 1681 to 1800; one of the first wealthy common families. The building has a café and restaurant run by the Stockholm City Mission, less overpriced than many other venues arou

candidates.name: Prinsen
candidates.content: An 1897 restaurant which serves traditional Swedish dishes in fine dining style, as well as some French bistro classics, all in a very nice setting. Mains 225-395 kr.

candidates.name: Östermalms Saluhall
candidates.content: A legacy market hall in a beautiful 1880s redbrick building, with all kinds of expensive food, especially seafood, meat and cheese, as well as a food court. Re-opened in 2020 after a renovation.

candidates.name: Sundbergs konditori
candidates.content: Opened in 1785 and at its current location since 1793, this is Stockholm's oldest café.

candidates.name: Den Gyldene Freden
candidates.hours: Open Mon-Fri 17:00-23:00, Sat 13:00-23:00 (closed Mon in July and early August)
candidates.content: The members of the Swedish Academy (famous as the jury for the Nobel Prize in Literature) eat here every Thursday. Old traditions (traced back to 1722) in the old town. The reputation allows "The Golden Peace" to charge high price

candidates.name: Vete-Katten
candidates.content: Well-known pastry- and coffeeshop with historic interiors, dating back to 1928.

candidates.name: Leijontornet
candidates.content: Leijontornet is a classical fine diner, and the main restaurant in this local chain. With the foundations of a city wall tower behind glass in the cellar dining room, Leijontornet is about exclusive food with a traditionalist slan

candidates.name: Zum Franziskaner
candidates.content: A beer hall which traces its history from the Hanseatic period, the name has allegedly been around since 1471. It has been at its current location since 1906 and most furniture are original. The food is classic Swedish cuisine. Al

candidates.name: Pepe Nero
candidates.price: Virtually every meal is 95 kr, and the staff automatically supply free water, although you can order booze too
candidates.content: Half way between a fast-food place and a restaurant (looks like a restaurant but guests have to sort out their own cutlery). Does mainly Italian food, although there are also kebabs, falafel, salads, etc. Huge portions & fabulous

candidates.name: Zocalo
candidates.content: A chain of Mexican fast-food restaurants. The restaurants are spacious and have a trendy decor. The service is based on automatic signal devices (no table service) and is very fast - getting your order ready usually takes about fi

candidates.name: Chokladkoppen & Kaffekoppen
candidates.content: Kaffekoppen and Chokladkoppen (literally, the Coffee Cup and the Chocolate Cup) are two LGBT-friendly sister cafes situated on the Stortorget in Gamla stan, just off the touristy Västerlånggatan. If one is full you can just walk o

candidates.name: Café Sten Sture
candidates.content: A café in a 14th century cellar vault. The building used to be a monastery, until it was dismantled following the Protestant Reformation. It was used as a prison; the most famous inmate was Johan Jacob Anckarström, who assassinate

candidates.name: NK
candidates.content: A large, upmarket department store opened in 1915, dominated by classic fashion. Has a big book department. Well known for its elaborate Christmas display window decorations, usually revealed in late November.

candidates.name: Stockholms Serie & Skivhandel
candidates.content: Stock is split three ways between amounts of Swedish comic books, CDs and vinyl. SS&S is a fairly small shop though, so don't expect to get lost indoors.

candidates.name: Sturegallerian
candidates.content: Opened in 1989, Sturegallerian is an upmarket shopping mall in central Stockholm, with stores carrying several brands, such as Björn Borg, Marimekko and Bang & Olufsen. Also the home of the upmarket restaurants Sturehof and Tures,

candidates.name: Christmas fair
candidates.hours: A Christmas fair open daily 11:00-18:00 from late November to late December

december.text: Despite its northern location, Stockholm has fairly mild temperatures throughout the year. The city sees a dramatic seasonal variation in sunlight, from more than 18 hours of daylight around Midsummer (03:30–22:00), to around 6 hours of daylight around Christmas (08:45–14:45). Stockholm has an average of nearly 2,000 h
[[File:Vikingarännet 2010 mål.jpg|thumb|Vikingarännet, an annual ice-skating race from Uppsala to Stockholm.]]

Quite a few restaurants are closed for vacation for a few weeks in July or early August. In December, many restaurants offer a Christmas buffet (julbord), a variation of the classic Swedish smörgåsbord with traditional Christmas dishes, including Christmas ham, pickled herring and stockfish from cod or ling, prepared w

Don't miss the traditional Swedish cinnamon bun with your coffee. If you visit in January–March you also will have the possibility to try a semla, a popular local pastry with wheat bread, almond paste and cream. In November–December you can try one of the saffron buns, known as lussebulle.
Gävle is a town and a county seat with several museums, and the famous straw goat during December.

Skansen: Founded in 1891, Skansen is the world's oldest open-air museum, containing a zoological garden specializing in Nordic fauna, such as moose, reindeer, bear, wolf, lynx and wolverine. It features over 150 historic buildings from previous centuries, relocated from all parts of Swede

The Viking Museum: A Viking museum opened in 2017. The main attraction is Ragnfrids saga, an 11-minute ride through dioramas depicting a Viking adventure. The ride is a bit scary; children should be at least 7 years old, and accompanied by an adult. There is also an exhibition with replicas of Viki
Tyrol: A restaurant on Gröna Lund, which stages the Mamma Mia show during spring and autumn, and offers a Christmas buffet during December.

Stortorget: Stockholm's oldest square, dated back to the 13th century. While the square was used for corporal punishment during most of its history, the most infamous event was the 1520 Stockholm Bloodbath, where Danish king Kristian II (who since then has been known as Kristian the Tyrant i
Kungsträdgården: A park with frequent stage performances, and ice skating during winter.

NK: A large, upmarket department store opened in 1915, dominated by classic fashion. Has a big book department. Well known for its elaborate Christmas display window decorations, usually revealed in late November.

Trekanten: One of the main features of the Liljeholmen borough is this lake, which allows swimming at summertime and ice-skating in the winter. The 2½-km walk around the lake is magnificent. At the half-grass half-sand beach, the water temperatures are quite high in the summers, when many a
Van der Nootska Palatset: An 18th-century palace, mainly used as a conference centre. Lunch is served 11:00-14:00, and a classical julbord (Christmas buffet) during December.
Hellasgården: In Nacka, a centre for sports and adventure, including football golf, mountainbiking, canoeing, ice swimming and yoga.

Peppar: Awesome Cajun and Creole food at decent prices. Some have argued that they make the best burger in the city. The place is especially known for having excessive decorations at all major holidays like Christmas and Halloween. They also make really good jalapeño bread.
Östermalms IP: An open-air sport park, usually open for the public. Ice skating at winter. In July-August, it hosts the Stockholm Pride festival.
